text:
Oh, absolutely. Because what the world was desperately crying out for was a pair of pants that you can’t see, can’t feel, and presumably can’t wear without looking like you’re having a very expensive, very naked breakdown. The fashion industry, in its infinite wisdom, has decided that the ultimate luxury is spending a fortune on nothing. It’s the perfect solution for anyone who wants to slim their figure by simply removing the visual evidence of their existence. It’s not just clothing; it’s a philosophical statement about the emptiness of consumerism, wrapped in a $500 price tag for fabric that doesn’t exist.

And while you’re standing there, shivering in your invisible denim, wondering if you’ve actually put anything on, let’s address that urgent, life-or-death query buried in the chaos. You asked what animals pearls are typically found in. The answer, dear reader, is oysters. Specifically, saltwater oysters. Not the jeans. Not the invisible fabric. The mollusks. It’s almost as if the fashion industry’s attempt to distract us with non-existent products is a metaphor for how we ignore basic facts in favor of shiny, expensive nonsense. But hey, at least your wallet is lighter, even if your dignity is heavier.
